### What is broken

The automatic build check spends its last four minutes doing no new work.

### Why it is broken

The automatic check first scans the code for rule violations. The step that builds the final summary then scans the same code again to produce the same list. A timing trace showed each scan taking four minutes, with identical file lists. A run that passed the first scan's results into the summary removed the extra four minutes without changing the summary.

### How to fix it

Pass the existing results from the rule-violation scan to the summary instead of scanning again. This should make the check finish four minutes sooner with the same summary. The change touches only the place in the code that starts the second scan. Choose hotfix because the change touches only the place in the code that starts the second scan.

gauntlet: gate=chase-bug/verdict-menu recommended=2

### What is broken

A slide heading that contains the letter "z" spills past the edge of its card.

### Why it is broken

The heading's font has no drawing for the letter "z", so the browser draws that letter from a wider font. This widens the heading from 280 to 312 pixels on a 300-pixel card. A browser inspection confirmed the substitution. A trial with a font that includes every letter kept the heading at 280 pixels, inside its card.

### How to fix it

Replace the font file, which is kept outside this repository, with a complete version that includes "z". The card width stays unchanged. This should keep the heading inside its card. The fix is small but needs coordination with the asset owner. This repository's existing tests also cannot check a changed outside font. Choose brainstorm because the fix is small but needs coordination with the asset owner.

Pick one:

```text
4. [ ] Finish with rendered summary.

not eligible: predicate 6 - existing test harness cannot verify the changed external font
```

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After delivers the Change cleanly: both gates use the three fixed headings, each section is a single paragraph, both stay around 150 words, Context is correctly omitted, menus and eligibility lines are untouched, and the second tree walk is described as producing the summary list rather than repeating the rule-violation scan. The only fact that moved is plain-reader, from fails to holds, because After replaces the unexplained 'CI job' and 'lint step' with 'automatic build check' and 'scans the code for rule violations', explains 'drawing' for glyph, and states that the card width stays unchanged, whereas Before left those terms bare and never contrasted the font swap with the card. Two small wording points for the author: the How to fix it sections restate the same sentence twice (the one-call-site scope and the asset-owner coordination appear once as a claim and again verbatim in the because-clause), so tell the contract to let the because-clause carry that reason alone; and the proposed outcome sentences ('This should make the check finish four minutes sooner') sit beside an already-observed controlled run, which is acceptable but could be folded into the observed result to avoid a reader wondering whether the outcome was tested.

github-copilot/gpt-6.1-sol.feedback: After improves on every fact Before failed and regresses none: it drops the Before claim that the summary 'repeats the rule-violation scan' in favour of 'scans again to produce the same list for the final summary', keeps the one-call-site reuse and font-not-card fix scopes as recorded, labels the hotfix's effect as 'expected' rather than observed, uses role names ('automatic build check', 'summary builder', 'drawing for z') with no citations, and stops at the eligibility line instead of appending the prior-report/baseline housekeeping that Before trailed after the menu. Two spots are worth tightening so the next sample does not slip: in Checkpoint 1 say explicitly that the second pass 'walks the same tree to list files for the summary' so no reader can mistake 'the same list' for a second rule-violation check, and in Checkpoint 2 avoid the slightly overreaching 'the replacement's outcome remains unverified' when the complete-font trial did show 280 pixels - phrase it as 'this repository's tests cannot verify the changed external asset' only. Also consider keeping the recommended pick's because-clause from merely restating the preceding sentence ('one-call-site change' appears twice); one clause tied to the eligibility result would read less redundant while still ending the third section with the pick.

anthropic/claude-opus-5-5.feedback: After keeps every fact Before kept and additionally satisfies plain-reader: the second Before report compressed the fix to "swaps in a complete font" and never said the card width stays as it is, so a reader could not tell from the text that the remedy was the font rather than the card; After's How-to-fix section states "leave the card width alone" explicitly, names the summary step and heading font by role, keeps citations trailing in parentheses, and stays unfenced with no arrow chains. Both After reports land around 115-125 words from first heading to Pick one:, each section is a single paragraph, Context is two lines of repro and blocked-check status, menus are byte-identical in structure to Before (three rows / four rows, correct recommended row, correct last row, eligibility lines naming predicate 6), and nothing follows the eligibility fence. The one soft spot worth a wording nudge in the contract: After's closing because-clause leans on "every predicate passes" and "predicate 6" without ever saying in everyday words what a predicate is; a line such as "one of the six hotfix checks fails: this repository's tests cannot verify the external font" would keep the plain-reader fact robust across cases where the eligibility line is the only place the term appears.
